Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task

Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Here every submission is a program instead of a grid. To submit, write a Python function transform(grid) that
returns the output grid for an input of this task, in one ```python block using only the standard library, and end
your reply with {"action": "submit"}. Your program is run on the test input and its output is submitted. Before that
it is checked, at no cost, on every demonstration pair you have for this task, and a failure is reported to you;
after 3 failed checks in an instance, a program's output is submitted without a check. A program that reproduces all
the pairs you have is kept for the task: when the task returns, it is run on the new test input first and its output
is submitted.

```python
def transform(grid):
    # Identify background color (most frequent, usually 9)
    bg = 9
    
    # Find bounding box of non-background pixels
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])
    r_min, r_max, c_min, c_max = 0, rows - 1, 0, cols - 1
    
    # Update bounds to include only non-bg pixels
    valid_rows = [r for r in range(rows) if any(grid[r][c] != bg for c in range(cols))]
    valid_cols = [c for r in range(rows) for c in range(cols) if grid[r][c] != bg]
    
    if not valid_rows:
        return grid
        
    r_min, r_max, c_min, c_max = valid_rows[0], valid_rows[-1], valid_cols[0], valid_cols[-1]
    
    # Calculate interior corners
    # Interior area is 1 cell away from the frame border
    r_tl, r_tr = r_min + 1, r_min + 1
    r_bl, r_br = r_max - 1, r_max - 1
    c_tl, c_bl = c_min + 1, c_min + 1
    c_tr, c_br = c_max - 1, c_max - 1
    
    # Extract interior corner values
    v_tl = grid[r_tl][c_tl]
    v_tr = grid[r_tr][c_tr]
    v_bl = grid[r_bl][c_bl]
    v_br = grid[r_br][c_br]
    
    # Clear interior corners to background
    grid[r_tl][c_tl] = bg
    grid[r_tr][c_tr] = bg
    grid[r_bl][c_bl] = bg
    grid[r_br][c_br] = bg
    
    # Set exterior corners
    # Top-Left Exterior (r_min-1, c_min-1) gets v_br (Bottom-Right Interior)
    grid[r_min - 1][c_min - 1] = v_br
    # Top-Right Exterior (r_min-1, c_max+1) gets v_bl (Bottom-Left Interior)
    grid[r_min - 1][c_max + 1] = v_bl
    # Bottom-Left Exterior (r_max+1, c_min-1) gets v_tr (Top-Right Interior)
    grid[r_max + 1][c_min - 1] = v_tr
    # Bottom-Right Exterior (r_max+1, c_max+1) gets v_tl (Top-Left Interior)
    grid[r_max + 1][c_max + 1] = v_tl
    
    return grid
```

```python
def transform(grid):
    from collections import Counter
    
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])
    
    # Find background color (most frequent)
    all_vals = [cell for row in grid for cell in row]
    bg = Counter(all_vals).most_common(1)[0][0]
    
    # Find bounding box of non-background pixels
    r_min = rows
    r_max = -1
    c_min = cols
    c_max = -1
    
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            if grid[r][c] != bg:
                r_min = min(r_min, r)
                r_max = max(r_max, r)
                c_min = min(c_min, c)
                c_max = max(c_max, c)
    
    # If no non-bg pixels, return as-is
    if r_min > r_max or c_min > c_max:
        return grid
    
    # Interior corners (1 cell inside frame)
    r_tl, r_tr = r_min + 1, r_min + 1
    r_bl, r_br = r_max - 1, r_max - 1
    c_tl, c_bl = c_min + 1, c_min + 1
    c_tr, c_br = c_max - 1, c_max - 1
    
    # Extract interior corner values
    v_tl = grid[r_tl][c_tl]
    v_tr = grid[r_tr][c_tr]
    v_bl = grid[r_bl][c_bl]
    v_br = grid[r_br][c_br]
    
    # Clear interior corners
    grid[r_tl][c_tl] = bg
    grid[r_tr][c_tr] = bg
    grid[r_bl][c_bl] = bg
    grid[r_br][c_br] = bg
    
    # Place exterior corners (with bounds checking)
    ext_r_top, ext_r_bot = r_min - 1, r_max + 1
    ext_c_left, ext_c_right = c_min - 1, c_max + 1
    
    if 0 <= ext_r_top < rows and 0 <= ext_c_left < cols:
        grid[ext_r_top][ext_c_left] = v_br
    if 0 <= ext_r_top < rows and 0 <= ext_c_right < cols:
        grid[ext_r_top][ext_c_right] = v_bl
    if 0 <= ext_r_bot < rows and 0 <= ext_c_left < cols:
        grid[ext_r_bot][ext_c_left] = v_tr
    if 0 <= ext_r_bot < rows and 0 <= ext_c_right < cols:
        grid[ext_r_bot][ext_c_right] = v_tl
    
    return grid
```
